EXPLANATION: The dominant 2220 cm⁻¹ band is characteristic of an aromatic nitrile C≡N stretch, matching benzonitrile derivatives. The presence of a clear high-frequency X–H band at 3376 cm⁻¹ and a strong band at 1605 cm⁻¹ fits an –NH₂ substituent (N–H stretch and bend; GFQ-002), which distinguishes p-aminobenzonitrile from halogen-only nitriles (e.g., 6, 10). The 847 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with para-disubstituted benzene out-of-plane C–H bending, and 3073 cm⁻¹ corresponds to aromatic C–H stretching (GFQ-003). Absence of an alkyne C≡C stretch near ~2100 cm⁻¹ disfavors candidates with C#C (1, 3, 5, 9).
